item.text:
**3B.9 Research Note**

Overall: **mixed but leaning negative**. Erdoğan’s government sometimes responded to acute flare-ups with order-restoring measures and relief, especially on the earthquake and anti-Syrian-riot episodes. But the broader pattern still includes protest crackdowns, censorship, and selective punishment, which cuts against a consistently protective or restraint-based crisis response.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | [Turkey completes new homes in area hit by devastating earthquake](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-completes-new-homes-in-area-hit-by-devastating-earthquake-3291916) | Reuters | 2024-02-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-completes-new-homes-in-area-hit-by-devastating-earthquake-3291916 | Erdoğan’s government handed over keys to 7,275 new homes to earthquake survivors in Hatay and said more deliveries were coming. This is real protective crisis response, though still framed as partially fulfilling a long-delayed reconstruction promise. | 3B.9 |
| Positive, mixed | [Protests and arrests as anti-Syrian riots rock Turkey](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/2/protests-and-arrests-as-anti-syrian-riots-rock-turkey) | Al Jazeera / Reuters | 2024-07-02 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/2/protests-and-arrests-as-anti-syrian-riots-rock-turkey | Erdoğan and Interior Minister Yerlikaya condemned anti-Syrian violence as unacceptable, and police detained more than 470 people. This is evidence of suppressing violence rather than tolerating it, though Erdoğan also blamed opposition parties for stoking tensions. | 3B.9; 3B.7; 3B.6 |
| Positive | [Turkey to open border gate for safe return of Syrians, Erdogan says](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-to-work-for-syrian-migrants-to-return-home-safely-minister-says-3760765) | Reuters | 2024-12-09 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-to-work-for-syrian-migrants-to-return-home-safely-minister-says-3760765 | Erdoğan said Turkey was opening the Yayladagi border gate to manage safe, voluntary return and prevent congestion after Assad’s fall. This is a restrained administrative response to a major displacement crisis. | 3B.9; 3B.7 |
| Negative | [Turkish police detain 210 May Day protesters in Istanbul, minister says](https://theprint.in/world/turkish-police-detain-217-may-day-protesters-in-istanbul-minister-says/2065973/) | Reuters | 2024-05-02 | https://theprint.in/world/turkish-police-detain-217-may-day-protesters-in-istanbul-minister-says/2065973/ | Erdoğan said May Day protests would not be allowed at Taksim Square; police used tear gas and rubber bullets and detained over 200 people. This is direct evidence of coercive handling of a spontaneous civic flare-up. | 3B.9; 3B.8; 3B.5 |
| Negative | [Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says authorities routinely banned gatherings critical of the government and police frequently used force against peaceful protests. That is a broader pattern of repression rather than crisis restraint. | 3B.9; 3B.8; 3B.5 |
| Negative | [Digital News Report 2024: Turkey](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report describes continued tight media control and legal changes that increased risk for journalists, activists, and ordinary citizens speaking online. That supports a censorship-heavy climate rather than transparent crisis management. | 3B.9; 3B.8; 3B.6 |

**Search gap**

I found some real protective responses, but I did **not** find strong evidence that Erdoğan consistently handled domestic crises without retaliatory pressure, censorship, or selective punishment. The positive examples are mostly **earthquake relief, riot policing, and migrant-management administration**; the broader pattern still points to a coercive political climate.
